scope: Every refusal OpenFGA constructs in `sources` is disposed below.

The enumeration is mechanical -- four rules, in `scripts/write-gate-causes.mjs` -- and its recall over those files is 100%, enforced by the residue check: every error-construction site in them is attributed to a key, or listed in `excluded` with a reason. That is what makes the count below mean anything.

It is not a claim that these files are upstream's whole refusal vocabulary. The protovalidate field constraints on the generated protobuf types are a real refusal layer living in a different Go module, which is not in the checkout and cannot be grepped; they are entered under `probes`, by measurement against the running container, and their completeness is not claimed.

The file set itself was widened once by measurement rather than by reading: running the conformance suite with `TSFGA_REFUSAL_LOG` set recorded two user-visible refusals -- the condition compile failure and the parameter type error -- that no file then in scope constructed. `internal/condition/errors.go` and rule R4 are that measurement's result.
`n/a` means 'not a rule of tsfga's write gate'. Where the refusal is implemented somewhere else -- the check path, an envelope around causes disposed on their own rows -- the reason says where.

causes.gap: only the one form a single config decides -- a relation whose sole arm is a tuple-to-userset onto itself over a tupleset admitting its own object type. The general rule is a whole-model property, which a per-config gate cannot decide.

`hasEntrypoints` traverses direct assignment and tuple-to-userset across types, so the general 'nothing can ever satisfy this relation' rule is a whole-model property. At a per-config gate it would refuse ordinary models whose relations are written in definition order rather than dependency order -- measured on this repo's own corpus. The pure-rewrite subset of it is the cycle rule.
